_note: Human-reviewed, corrected version of language-drafts.json (the raw Gemini output). This is the file actually merged into backend/data/venues.json and backend/services/retriever.js. See README's 'Expanding Language Coverage' section for the corrections made and why.

keywords.transit: ÖPNV Zug Bus U-Bahn letzte Abfahrt

reviewNotes: Deduped 'kann nicht atmen', which the draft repeated (mirroring the English list's "can't breathe"/"cant breathe" apostrophe-variant duplication, which doesn't carry over meaningfully once translated).
Replaced 'Angriff' (assault) with 'Übergriff': 'Angriff' is also the standard German football term for an attacking play, so a fan commentating on the match would falsely trigger an escalation.
Fixed all multi-word keyword strings, which the raw draft returned with no spaces between words (e.g. 'ToiletteWCBadezimmer'), making them unmatchable against any real tokenized query.
Corrected 'transit' keywords: the raw draft included 'Fahrrad' (bicycle), which doesn't fit the intended 'train' category — replaced with 'Zug' (train).

keywords.transit: trasporti treno bus metro ultima corsa

reviewNotes: Deduped 'non respiro', which the draft repeated (same apostrophe-variant artifact as German).
Added feminine 'bambina persa'/'bambina smarrita' — the draft only had masculine 'bambino' forms; Spanish/Portuguese in the existing data already carry both genders for this trigger.

'arma' (weapon) is a substring of 'armadio' (wardrobe/closet) — the same class of risk as the original Spanish 'arma'/'armario' bug. No fix needed here: the word-boundary-aware token matching already handles this correctly for any language, since 'arma' and 'armadio' are distinct tokens. Added a regression test to lock this in explicitly for Italian too.

keywords.transit: مواصلات قطار حافلة مترو آخر رحلة

reviewNotes: Not corrected, but flagged as an open question for a native speaker: 'طبية' is the feminine adjective form of "medical" and may not catch masculine-form phrasings of the same concept. Reviewed to the best of non-native confidence; everything else in this list reads as natural and correctly gendered (e.g. 'طفل ضائع'/'طفلة مفقودة' already covers both genders for lost/missing child).

keywords.wheelchairAccessible: 車椅子 バリアフリー
keywords.transit: 電車 バス 地下鉄 終電

reviewNotes: Fixed a real mistranslation: the draft's '子供がいない' literally means "I don't have children" (an entirely ordinary thing to say, e.g. when asking about family ticket policies) — not "lost child". Replaced with '子供がいなくなった' (the child has gone missing/disappeared), distinct from the adjacent, correctly-translated '子供が迷子' (the child is lost).

Stripped the romanized readings the draft appended in parentheses (e.g. '(guai ga warui)') — useful for a non-Japanese-fluent reviewer, but a real query won't contain the romaji, so keeping it in the stored trigger would prevent any match at all.

Japanese has no whitespace word segmentation, so unlike the other three languages, exact whitespace-token matching cannot work here at all — see the character-level fallback and its documented limitations in retriever.js and classifier.js.
